label: D2 after choosing a1 and landing in S2 (rare), when the policy is not strongly committed to a1
explanation: Fires only at D2 and only on the rare a1->S2 transition (in_action=a1, in_state=S2): that conjunction covers 99.99% of activations and mass but only 37% of such steps are active. The gate is the model own a1-vs-a2 logit at that D2 step: active when the logit is below ~1.5 (not strongly preferring a1). Adding choice<1.5 gives dev P 0.78 / R 0.86 / F1 0.82 / mass 0.93. The choice logit is the model own readout at that step, so it is observed, not future. Magnitude is largest when the recent history favoured a2 / S2 was good (top windows: a2 run, then a switch to a1 that rarely lands in S2, often rewarded at the next D1), meaning a rare transition into the state the agent already believes is good. Never fires at D1 or GO, on common transitions, or on a2->S1 rare transitions. A strong a1 preference (S1 believed good) suppresses it.

issues: Factual claims hold. On the dev split, 0 of 17084 active steps fall at D1 or GO and 0 have in_action=a2 (so a2 rare transitions never fire). Exactly 1 active step has state S1 / common. (phase==D2)&(action==1)&(state==2) has recall 1.0, mass recall 1.0 and precision 0.374.

Test scores reproduce: P 0.79, R 0.85, F1 0.819, mass recall 0.921. The threshold of 1.5 is close to optimal: a cutoff of 1.7 gives test F1 0.806, and on dev a cutoff of 1.0 gives coverage 0.75 / 0.92 in the low and top activation quartiles.

The suppression claim is supported. Within the base conjunction, steps with choice>=1.5 have precision only 0.089 and hold 7% of the mass. On test, the false positives are mostly long runs of rewarded a1 choices, i.e. a strongly committed a1 policy.
The missed activations are weak (mostly relative activation 0.00-0.15) and scattered. They hold 7.9% of the mass and form no systematic class.

Caveat on circularity: 'choice' at D2 is the policy readout of the same hidden state that this candidate feature feeds into, so 'not strongly committed to a1' is partly a downstream correlate of the feature rather than an independent cause. Observed-history proxies do much worse: excluding a previous rewarded a1 gives test F1 0.43-0.48. So the label is best read as a description of the agent's belief state, not as an observed-history predicate.

The magnitude claim is weakly supported but overstated in emphasis. good==2 covers 19% of the top activation quartile vs 11% of the bottom quartile, and precision is higher there (0.54 vs 0.36). But most activation mass (77%) falls on good==S1 trials, because a1 is chosen more often when S1 is good.
